note:
1.4.1 for the tenants tier. This tier carries 1.3.1, so a claw here crosses two
releases in one apply and 1.4.0 is the skipped one. The run back-fills one
changelog entry for 1.4.0 below 1.4.1's own. Class fix. Disruption quiet:
neither core floor moves, codex stays at 0.147.0 and claude at 2.1.227.

This is a large landing, because 1.4.0 installs rails a claw at 1.3.1 does not
have at all. It seeds /etc/orchestrate.conf, adds a swapfile sized to the box
with an out-of-memory guard, installs the memory check and the stall check with
their timers, installs the notifier and the wake rail, and creates the
notification state directory. 1.4.1 then adds the operator runbook, the health
reading, and the fixes below. A claw taking this crosses from having none of
that to having all of it in one run.

1.4.0's landing section has to be read, because a claw crossing it never meets
it through the rail. It asks for two things and neither one fails a run. Put
this claw's channel webhook into its vault, or the memory alarm and the stall
report run, find what they find, and nothing leaves the box. And enrol this
claw's dead-man check, which is one command on the operator's side and one on
the claw. Until both halves are done the five-minute beat skips the ping in
silence: no error, no noise, and no off-box cover.

The box half. Only one claw on this channel was measured for this note, on
2026-09-02 at 16:38 UTC. It holds two people in claw-members, both with a
persistent core at 2.1.227, which meets the floor, and the per-task core at its
floor with the companion host present. So no member there reads as below a
floor and that claw's own classifier will not defer. Every other claw on this
channel measures itself the same way before it rides: one read of the members
group, and one look at each member's launcher. A member who has never signed in
reads as below the floor whatever the releases say, and that alone defers a
release to the quiet window.

Three things this release changes about riding one.

The claw-admin door phase now proves its scope where the scope is written. It
used to prove it by asking what a member may run, and on a claw with wide mode
on the honest answer is everything, so three checks failed and the whole apply
stopped. This is the release that makes a wide-mode claw able to take a release
at all. A claw with wide mode off still gets the live refusal pair.

The health line at the end of an apply is now scripts/unit-health.sh and it has
two halves: nothing failed, and nothing in activating carrying a restart count.
An empty systemctl --failed on its own is no longer the reading, because a unit
with Restart= never settles into failed and the old line called a looping box
healthy.

The wake rail's per-account unit no longer fails when that account has nobody
signed in. It idles, says so once, and delivers when a session opens. Before
this release that state exited the unit, systemd restarted it every ten
seconds, and the failed unit took the whole apply down. One caution the notes
do not carry: the rail decides a session is reachable by finding the account's
socket directory, not by counting what is in it, so an account that has signed
in once and left reads as reachable and the nudge goes to nobody. Nothing
fails. It is a nudge that does not arrive.

The updater fix in a release lands one release late, because the apply is
performed by the updater the claw already has. So this apply prints no
end-of-run health line, and the reading arrives from the next update. Running
scripts/unit-health.sh by hand works the moment this release lands.

The operator runbook lands at /opt/commonclaw/doc/operator-runbook.md on every
claw that takes this release.
